title: When the Contact Sings
premise: Noor Nystrom, a private security contractor who has spent a decade keeping clients alive by staying off every record, is guarding a whistleblower mid-flight when the aircraft's manifest, transponder history, and passenger logs are erased in real time—while the plane is still airborne. The vanished flight was carrying evidence that three governments conspired to bury an assassination planned for the upcoming Baltic summit, and Noor realizes his own decade of invisible work made him the perfect fall guy. Hunted across Copenhagen, Riga, and Stockholm by an assassin who knows his tradecraft because she trained beside him, Noor must decide whether loyalty to the handler who saved his life matters more than the truth. He gets the evidence to the summit floor at the cost of his anonymity forever, exposing the plot but ending the only life he knew how to live.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime security consultant who spent eight years writing risk assessments for clients she still cannot name. She lives on the Baltic coast, where she watches cargo planes and takes notes.

chapters.title: Manifest of One
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A routine protection detail aboard a chartered flight from Copenhagen to Riga, escorting a nervous data analyst named Ilze Berzins. Noor notices the cabin crew list has one name too few. Emotional beat: professional unease—the first crack in a world he thought he understood.

chapters.title: The Plane That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Mid-flight, Ilze shows him her encrypted drive; minutes later the cockpit confirms their transponder code no longer exists in any registry. They land at a military strip where no one is expecting them. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground itself feels unreliable.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Noor's POV recalling how his handler, Marcus Vane, recruited him after a botched embassy job, teaching him that survival means leaving no trace. Present-day Vane orders him to hand over Ilze and forget the flight. Emotional beat: the pull of debt and gratitude.

chapters.title: Ilze's Drive
chapters.summary: Ilze's POV via recovered recording. She explains what's on the drive: intercepted communications proving a summit assassination will be blamed on a fabricated terrorist cell—one built from real contractors' files, including Noor's. Emotional beat: dread becoming personal.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. He stashes Ilze in a Riga safehouse and runs counter-surveillance, discovering a tail who moves exactly like someone from his old training cohort. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Knew His Name
chapters.summary: Mara Kessler's POV introduced. The assassin reviews Noor's file—not from intelligence channels but from memory—and we learn they trained together under Vane before she was burned. Emotional beat: cold nostalgia masking something unresolved.

chapters.title: Burn Notice in Reverse
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. His accounts freeze, his cover identities expire simultaneously, and an Interpol flag appears with his face attached to the vanished flight. Someone is building him into the patsy file in real time. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is the quarry.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating brief POVs: a Danish intelligence officer ordered to stand down, a Latvian border chief deleting records, a Swedish minister's aide receiving instructions. Emotional beat: institutional rot seen from inside three offices at once.

chapters.title: Riga Nightfall
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Mara finds the safehouse. Instead of killing him she gives him ninety seconds to run, and Ilze escapes through drainage tunnels while Noor draws the pursuit. Emotional beat: betrayal and mercy tangled together.

chapters.title: What Vane Owes
chapters.summary: Noor confronts Vane in Gdansk. Vane admits the operation is real but claims surrendering the drive is the only way Noor survives, invoking the debt from Chapter 3. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Ilze's POV. Hiding aboard a passenger ferry to Stockholm, she decrypts a second layer of the drive revealing the assassin's target: not a head of state, but the summit's arbitration chair—the one man who could audit all three governments. Emotional beat: the stakes doubling.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds Longer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her handlers order her to finish both targets; she stalls, fabricating surveillance reports, and we see her begin keeping her own invisible ledger. Emotional beat: the first act of treason, quiet as paperwork.

chapters.title: Stockholm Static
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Reunited with Ilze, he contacts a journalist who once owed Vane a favor, only to find the newsroom already compromised. Emotional beat: every door closing except the ones that lead deeper in.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Following a clue in the erased flight data, he locates a Cold War-era records vault where the original assassination contract was drafted—signed by an official whose name appears in all three governments' chains of command. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He wrote Noor's file into the patsy plan years ago as insurance, believing a controllable scapegoat was kinder than a dead contractor. Emotional beat: the mentor revealed as architect, love indistinguishable from use.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. With the summit hours away, Noor, Ilze, and the half-turned Mara pool what they have: the drive, the vault documents, and Mara's access codes. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, three people betting everything on each other.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Infiltrating the summit venue through service tunnels, they trigger lockdowns to reach the arbitration chamber while Mara feeds false positions to her handlers. Emotional beat: controlled terror, tradecraft as prayer.

chapters.title: Contact Singing
chapters.summary: Climax. Mara's handlers discover her betrayal; she holds the corridor alone so Noor can reach the chamber, taking a fatal wound. Noor broadcasts the archive documents to every delegate terminal as guards breach. Emotional beat: sacrifice converting silence into signal.

chapters.title: The Chair Decides
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The arbitration chair suspends the summit and opens a public inquiry; delegates scatter, denials cascade, but the documents are irreversibly out. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Ilze's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilze's POV. Testifying under protection, she insists Noor be named as witness, not suspect, forcing the inquiry to acknowledge the man the files erased. Emotional beat: memory restored by another's courage.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Vane, exposed but protected by old alliances, offers Noor a new identity and a clean slate—the same gift that was always a cage. Noor declines. Emotional beat: refusing survival at the price of self.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. Months later, Noor testifies openly, his name in transcripts for the first time in ten years. He visits Mara's unmarked grave on the Baltic coast and finally books a flight under his own name. Emotional beat: the price paid, the self reclaimed.
